subject: Holiday traffic: request for temporary p95 measurement carveout and fallback commitments
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@finlytics.io>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <carlos@finlytics.io>
Date: 2026-09-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Holiday surge — p95 carveout / measurement window question

Hi Rachel,

Hope youre well. Were planning for an unusually large marketing-driven traffic surge over Black Friday week and want to understand whether Redwood can provide a short-term accommodation on hosted API latency SLOs.

Specifically: can we request a temporary modification to p95 measurement (shorter rolling window or a transient carveout for a 7-day window) so that our contractual p95 doesnt trigger credits for predictable, short-lived marketing peaks? Were willing to accept stricter fallbacks (lower throughput tier / model downgrade) during those days if thats required.

Two asks from our side:
- A clear proposal for the exact measurement change (windowing or grace) and how long it would apply.
- A plan for observability/evidence we can both use to verify the spike nature (sampled traces, KV cache hit graphs, and token-level latency distribution).

Can you point us to how Redwood typically handles these temporary exceptions, and whether this is contract-amendment territory or an operational carveout?

Thanks,
Samantha
Head of Platform, FinLytics

---
Attachment: marketing-forecast-fall2026.csv (stub)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@finlytics.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-04T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Holiday surge — p95 carveout / measurement window question

Hi Samantha — thanks for the note and the heads-up. Quick reply with how we usually approach this and a proposal attached.

High-level: we prefer operational carveouts where possible (short-term measurement window adjustments + transient grace) rather than changing baseline contractual SLAs. That keeps long-term commitments intact while preventing noisy marketing spikes from creating credit events.

Proposal summary (attached PDF has full detail):
- Temporary window: 7-day carveout starting at the requested UTC date. During that window, p95 is computed with a transient grace that excludes the top 5% of the most intense 1-minute buckets for the day (effective at reducing creditable p95 noise).
- Fallbacks: during the window we can automatically route up to 30% of traffic to a lower-cost model variant (quantized q4_0) with a documented expected p95 uplift; this is application-configurable on your end.
- Evidence: we will provide a daily digest (sampled traces, prefix-KV hit rate, per-region p50/p95 histograms) and a final 14-day post-window analysis.
- Governance: operational carveouts are executed via an amendment workflow: internal SRE sign-off + DocuSign acknowledgement by FinLytics. Kimberly, can you confirm the minimal legal language and whether this needs a PO amendment?

Ive attached the proposal and an evidence collection plan. If this looks right, we can run a 30-day pilot and instrument more granular traces during your peak.

Next step: quick call tomorrow 10am PT to confirm dates?

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: hosted-slo-carveout-proposal-sept2026.pdf; evidence-collection-plan-sept2026.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Samantha Lee <samantha@finlytics.io>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-04T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Holiday surge — p95 carveout / measurement window question

Adding some technical color from the runtime side. A few notes youll want to be aware of so expectations line up:

- Measurement effect: p95 is sensitive to short, dense bursts. Removing top 1-minute buckets (or applying a daily carveout) materially reduces false positives for credit triggers.
- Batching & KV cache: if FinLytics is using inference batching well need to know the client-side batch sizes / request burst profile. Also share whether prefix caching is expected; that affects the shape of p50/p95.
- Fallback model expectations: the q4_0 variant tends to add ~15-25ms to p50 and ~30-60ms to p95 depending on request length; we can publish expected deltas for your call patterns.
- Region routing: if you plan to burst across regions, please highlight which regions so we can exclude region-wide infra events from the evidence set.

Rachel — if we proceed, I recommend we lock the evidence collection schema in the first 48 hours of the pilot.

Ben
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Samantha Lee <samantha@finlytics.io>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Carlos Mendes <carlos@finlytics.io>
Date: 2026-09-05T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Holiday surge — p95 carveout / measurement window question

Thanks Rachel and Ben — this is exactly what we needed. A couple clarifications from our side:

- Wed prefer the operational carveout approach.
- Requesting the carveout window to be Nov 25, 2026 — Nov 30, 2026 (local times) to cover our campaign period.
- Pilot: wed like the pilot to run for 30 days (Nov 1  Nov 30) so we capture pre-peak baseline and the full ramp.
- Batching: we use client-side batching (peak batch size ~8) and prefix caching is ON for 60% of traffic. Region: US-west + EU-central.

Kimberly — what contractual acknowledgement do you need? Were fine signing an operational amendment; prefer not to modify the master SLA if possible.

Samantha

Samantha — thanks, that timeline and pilot look reasonable. A few legal/ops items to close before we kick off instrumentation:

1) Amendment: we will prepare a short operational amendment that references the existing SLA and states this as a time-bound operational carveout (effective dates, evidence obligations, rollback criteria). No permanent SLA change.
2) Evidence retention: Redwood will retain the daily evidence digest for 90 days; please confirm thats sufficient for your internal audit.
3) Fallback opt-in: include a toggle in the DocuSign so your platform team can choose whether automatic routing to the quantized variant is enabled during the window. If the toggle is OFF, we will use rate-limiting + queuing policies instead.
4) Acceptance criteria: post-window, if drifted p95 exceeds baseline + agreed threshold for >48 hours (excluding non-Redwood infra events), well execute a remediation playbook and credit policy per Section 4.3 of the SLA.

Next steps: Ill have our legal ops draft the amendment and send via DocuSign by EOD Monday. Rachel — please follow up with the proposal PDF link and the evidence schema so Samantha can share with their SREs.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Commercial Contracts, Redwood Inference
